note: Dated world events of the 2000s, generated by scripts/dev/gen-events-history.py from candidates verified against Wikipedia (scripts/research/verify-events.ts): the date of each was found in the cited article. Descriptions state documented facts only; effects are gameplay estimates from templates. Events fire only for listed countries that exist on the map; natural disasters and pandemics also fire in dynamic mode.

events.title: The dot-com peak
events.description: On 10 March 2000 the NASDAQ Composite index peaked; the dot-com bubble then burst.

events.title: Withdrawal from southern Lebanon
events.description: Israel withdrew its forces from southern Lebanon in May 2000.

events.title: ILOVEYOU virus
events.description: The ILOVEYOU computer worm spread around the world from 4 May 2000.

events.title: Operation Palliser
events.description: British forces deployed to Sierra Leone in May 2000.

source.title: Wikipedia: British military intervention in the Sierra Leone Civil War

events.title: Coup in Fiji
events.description: Armed men seized the Parliament of Fiji on 19 May 2000.

events.title: Inter-Korean summit
events.description: The leaders of South and North Korea met in Pyongyang from 13 to 15 June 2000.

events.title: Concorde crash
events.description: Air France Flight 4590, a Concorde, crashed shortly after take-off from Paris on 25 July 2000.

events.title: The Kursk
events.description: The Russian submarine Kursk sank in the Barents Sea on 12 August 2000 during a naval exercise.

events.title: Second Intifada
events.description: The Second Intifada began in late September 2000.

events.title: Protests in Belgrade
events.description: Mass protests in Belgrade on 5 October 2000 led to the fall of Slobodan Milošević.

events.title: USS Cole bombing
events.description: The destroyer USS Cole was attacked in the harbour of Aden, Yemen, on 12 October 2000.

events.title: Wikipedia launches
events.description: Wikipedia was launched on 15 January 2001.

events.title: Gujarat earthquake
events.description: An earthquake struck Gujarat, India, on 26 January 2001.

events.title: Financial crisis
events.description: A financial crisis hit Turkey in February 2001.

events.title: Foot-and-mouth outbreak
events.description: An outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease was confirmed in Britain on 19 February 2001.

events.title: The Buddhas of Bamiyan
events.description: The Taliban destroyed the Buddhas of Bamiyan in March 2001.

events.title: Hainan Island incident
events.description: A United States Navy surveillance aircraft and a Chinese fighter collided near Hainan Island on 1 April 2001.

events.title: Royal massacre
events.description: King Birendra and several members of the Nepalese royal family were killed at the palace on 1 June 2001.

events.title: Genoa G8 summit
events.description: The G8 summit in Genoa from 20 to 22 July 2001 was met by mass protests.

events.title: Assassination of Ahmad Shah Massoud
events.description: Ahmad Shah Massoud, commander of the Northern Alliance, was killed by suicide bombers on 9 September 2001.

events.title: Anthrax letters
events.description: Letters containing anthrax spores were mailed to news media offices and two senators from 18 September 2001.

events.title: WTO accession approved
events.description: The WTO Ministerial Conference approved China's accession in November 2001.

source.title: Wikipedia: China and the World Trade Organization

events.title: The corralito
events.description: On 1 December 2001 Argentina restricted cash withdrawals from bank accounts (the corralito).

events.title: Enron bankruptcy
events.description: Enron filed for bankruptcy on 2 December 2001.

events.title: Attack on the Indian Parliament
events.description: Militants attacked the Parliament of India in New Delhi on 13 December 2001.

events.title: Guantanamo detention camp
events.description: The first detainees arrived at the Guantanamo Bay detention camp on 11 January 2002.

events.title: Coup attempt in Venezuela
events.description: President Hugo Chávez was briefly removed from power on 11 April 2002 and restored two days later.

events.title: Shock first round
events.description: In the first round of the presidential election on 21 April 2002, Jean-Marie Le Pen came second and reached the runoff.

events.title: Assassination of Pim Fortuyn
events.description: Politician Pim Fortuyn was shot dead in Hilversum on 6 May 2002.

events.title: Independence of East Timor
events.description: East Timor became independent on 20 May 2002.

events.title: International Criminal Court
events.description: The Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court entered into force on 1 July 2002.

events.title: The African Union
events.description: The African Union was launched in Durban on 9 July 2002, replacing the Organisation of African Unity.

events.title: Floods in central Europe
events.description: Severe floods hit central Europe in August 2002.

events.title: Nuclear sites revealed
events.description: In August 2002 an Iranian opposition group revealed the existence of nuclear facilities at Natanz and Arak.

events.title: Bali bombings
events.description: Bombs exploded in the tourist district of Kuta, Bali, on 12 October 2002.

events.title: Moscow theatre siege
events.description: Armed militants seized a Moscow theatre on 23 October 2002 and took the audience hostage.

events.title: Prestige oil spill
events.description: The oil tanker Prestige broke up off the coast of Galicia in November 2002.

events.title: Columbia disaster
events.description: The Space Shuttle Columbia broke up on re-entry on 1 February 2003.

events.title: SARS
events.description: The World Health Organization issued a global alert about a severe atypical pneumonia, later named SARS, in March 2003.

events.title: Human Genome Project completed
events.description: The completion of the Human Genome Project was announced in April 2003.

events.title: Riyadh compound bombings
events.description: Suicide bombers attacked residential compounds in Riyadh on 12 May 2003.

events.title: Casablanca bombings
events.description: Suicide bombers attacked several sites in Casablanca on 16 May 2003.

events.title: Summer heatwave
events.description: A heatwave struck Europe in the summer of 2003.

events.title: End of the Liberian civil war
events.description: Charles Taylor resigned as President of Liberia in August 2003 and went into exile.

events.title: Northeast blackout
events.description: A power outage hit the northeastern United States and Ontario on 14 August 2003.

events.title: Assassination of Anna Lindh
events.description: Swedish Foreign Minister Anna Lindh was stabbed in Stockholm on 10 September 2003 and died the next day.

events.title: Euro referendum
events.description: Swedish voters rejected adopting the euro in a referendum on 14 September 2003.

events.title: First Chinese crewed spaceflight
events.description: Shenzhou 5 carried Yang Liwei into orbit on 15 October 2003, the first Chinese crewed spaceflight.

events.title: Concorde retired
events.description: Concorde made its last commercial flight on 24 October 2003.

events.title: Istanbul bombings
events.description: Truck bombs exploded in Istanbul on 15 and 20 November 2003.

events.title: Rose Revolution
events.description: Mass protests in Georgia led to the resignation of President Eduard Shevardnadze on 23 November 2003.

events.title: Capture of Saddam Hussein
events.description: United States forces captured Saddam Hussein near Tikrit on 13 December 2003.

events.title: Bam earthquake
events.description: An earthquake destroyed much of the city of Bam, Iran, on 26 December 2003.

events.title: Facebook launches
events.description: Facebook was launched on 4 February 2004.

events.title: Aristide leaves Haiti
events.description: President Jean-Bertrand Aristide left Haiti on 29 February 2004.

events.title: Madrid train bombings
events.description: Bombs exploded on commuter trains in Madrid on 11 March 2004, three days before the general election.

events.title: Athens Olympics
events.description: Athens hosted the Summer Olympics from 13 to 29 August 2004.

events.title: Beslan school siege
events.description: Armed militants seized a school in Beslan, North Ossetia, on 1 September 2004.

events.title: Chūetsu earthquake
events.description: An earthquake struck Niigata Prefecture, Japan, on 23 October 2004.

events.title: Murder of Theo van Gogh
events.description: Film director Theo van Gogh was murdered in Amsterdam on 2 November 2004.

events.title: Death of Yasser Arafat
events.description: Yasser Arafat died on 11 November 2004.

events.title: Orange Revolution
events.description: Mass protests over the presidential election runoff began in Ukraine in late November 2004.

events.title: Indian Ocean tsunami
events.description: An undersea earthquake off Sumatra on 26 December 2004 caused tsunamis around the Indian Ocean.

source.title: Wikipedia: 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami

events.title: Assassination of Rafic Hariri
events.description: Former Lebanese Prime Minister Rafic Hariri was killed by a bomb in Beirut on 14 February 2005.

events.title: YouTube launches
events.description: YouTube was founded on 14 February 2005.

events.title: Kyoto Protocol in force
events.description: The Kyoto Protocol on greenhouse gas emissions entered into force on 16 February 2005.

events.title: Cedar Revolution
events.description: Mass demonstrations in Beirut in March 2005 called for the withdrawal of Syrian troops from Lebanon.

events.title: Tulip Revolution
events.description: Protesters took over government buildings in Bishkek on 24 March 2005 and President Askar Akayev fled.

events.title: Death of Pope John Paul II
events.description: Pope John Paul II died on 2 April 2005.

events.title: Election of Pope Benedict XVI
events.description: Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger was elected Pope on 19 April 2005 and took the name Benedict XVI.

events.title: Andijan unrest
events.description: Security forces opened fire on protesters in Andijan, Uzbekistan, on 13 May 2005.

events.title: Referendum on the European Constitution
events.description: French voters rejected the Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe in a referendum on 29 May 2005.

events.title: Referendum on the European Constitution
events.description: Dutch voters rejected the Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe in a referendum on 1 June 2005.

events.title: London wins the Olympics
events.description: London was chosen on 6 July 2005 to host the 2012 Summer Olympics.

source.title: Wikipedia: London bid for the 2012 Summer Olympics

events.title: London bombings
events.description: Suicide bombers attacked London's public transport on 7 July 2005.

events.title: Sharm El Sheikh bombings
events.description: Bombs exploded in the Egyptian resort of Sharm El Sheikh on 23 July 2005.

events.title: Disengagement from Gaza
events.description: Israel began withdrawing its settlers and forces from the Gaza Strip in August 2005.

source.title: Wikipedia: Israeli disengagement from the Gaza Strip

events.title: Hurricane Katrina
events.description: Hurricane Katrina made landfall on the Gulf Coast of the United States on 29 August 2005; New Orleans was flooded.

events.title: Second Bali bombings
events.description: Suicide bombers attacked tourist sites in Bali on 1 October 2005.

events.title: EU accession talks open
events.description: Accession negotiations between Turkey and the European Union opened on 3 October 2005.

source.title: Wikipedia: Accession of Turkey to the European Union

events.title: Kashmir earthquake
events.description: An earthquake struck Kashmir on 8 October 2005.

events.title: Riots in the suburbs
events.description: Riots broke out in the suburbs of Paris on 27 October 2005 and spread to other French cities.

events.title: Amman hotel bombings
events.description: Suicide bombers attacked three hotels in Amman on 9 November 2005.

events.title: First woman Chancellor
events.description: Angela Merkel became Chancellor of Germany on 22 November 2005, the first woman in the office.

events.title: Gas cut to Ukraine
events.description: Russia cut gas supplies to Ukraine on 1 January 2006 in a dispute over prices.

events.title: Cartoons controversy
events.description: Protests over the Jyllands-Posten cartoons of Muhammad spread across many countries in early 2006.

events.title: Al-Askari mosque bombing
events.description: The al-Askari Shrine in Samarra was bombed on 22 February 2006.

events.title: Twitter launches
events.description: The first message was posted on Twitter in March 2006.

events.title: Yogyakarta earthquake
events.description: An earthquake struck the Yogyakarta region of Java in May 2006.

events.title: Montenegrin independence referendum
events.description: Montenegro voted for independence in a referendum on 21 May 2006.

events.title: World Cup in Germany
events.description: Germany hosted the FIFA World Cup from 9 June to 9 July 2006.

events.title: Islamic Courts take Mogadishu
events.description: The Islamic Courts Union took control of Mogadishu in June 2006.

events.title: World champions
events.description: Italy won the FIFA World Cup on 9 July 2006.

events.title: Mumbai train bombings
events.description: Bombs exploded on suburban trains in Mumbai on 11 July 2006.

events.title: Protests in Budapest
events.description: Protests broke out in Budapest in September 2006 after a leaked speech by Prime Minister Ferenc Gyurcsány.

events.title: Coup in Thailand
events.description: The Royal Thai Army overthrew the government of Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra on 19 September 2006.

events.title: North Korean nuclear test
events.description: North Korea conducted its first nuclear test on 9 October 2006.

events.title: Litvinenko poisoning
events.description: Alexander Litvinenko died in London in November 2006 after being poisoned with polonium-210.

events.title: Offensive against the cartels
events.description: The Mexican government deployed troops against drug cartels in Michoacán in December 2006.

events.title: Ethiopian intervention
events.description: Ethiopian forces intervened in Somalia in December 2006.

events.title: Execution of Saddam Hussein
events.description: Saddam Hussein was executed in Baghdad on 30 December 2006.

events.title: The iPhone
events.description: Apple introduced the iPhone on 9 January 2007.

events.title: Algiers bombings
events.description: Suicide bombers attacked the Prime Minister's office and a police station in Algiers on 11 April 2007.

events.title: Bronze Night
events.description: Riots broke out in Tallinn over the relocation of the Bronze Soldier of Tallinn in late April 2007, followed by cyberattacks on Estonia.

events.title: Glasgow Airport attack
events.description: A car loaded with gas canisters was driven into Glasgow Airport on 30 June 2007.

events.title: Credit crunch
events.description: Interbank lending markets froze in August 2007 as losses on US subprime mortgages spread.

events.title: Saffron Revolution
events.description: Protests led by Buddhist monks spread across Myanmar in August and September 2007.

events.title: Run on Northern Rock
events.description: Depositors queued to withdraw their savings from Northern Rock from 14 September 2007.

events.title: State of emergency
events.description: President Pervez Musharraf declared a state of emergency in Pakistan on 3 November 2007.

events.title: Treaty of Lisbon signed
events.description: The leaders of the European Union signed the Treaty of Lisbon on 13 December 2007.

events.title: Assassination of Benazir Bhutto
events.description: Former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 27 December 2007.

events.title: Post-election crisis
events.description: Violence broke out in Kenya after the presidential election result was announced on 30 December 2007.

events.title: Fidel Castro steps down
events.description: Fidel Castro announced in February 2008 that he would not accept another term as President of Cuba.

events.title: Kosovo declares independence
events.description: The Assembly of Kosovo declared independence from Serbia on 17 February 2008.

events.title: Unrest in Tibet
events.description: Riots and protests broke out in Lhasa and other Tibetan areas in March 2008.

events.title: Cyclone Nargis
events.description: Cyclone Nargis struck Myanmar on 2 May 2008.

events.title: Sichuan earthquake
events.description: An earthquake struck Sichuan province, China, on 12 May 2008.

events.title: Oil at record prices
events.description: The price of oil reached a record high in July 2008.

events.title: Large Hadron Collider
events.description: The Large Hadron Collider at CERN first circulated a beam on 10 September 2008.

events.title: Icelandic banking collapse
events.description: Iceland's three largest banks collapsed in October 2008.

events.title: Bank rescue
events.description: The Emergency Economic Stabilization Act, creating the Troubled Asset Relief Program, became law on 3 October 2008.

events.title: Bank rescue package
events.description: The British government announced a rescue package for the banking system on 8 October 2008.

source.title: Wikipedia: 2008 United Kingdom bank rescue package

events.title: Mumbai attacks
events.description: Militants carried out coordinated shooting and bombing attacks across Mumbai from November 2008.

events.title: Hyperinflation
events.description: Inflation in Zimbabwe reached its peak in November 2008.

events.title: Riots in Greece
events.description: Riots broke out in Greece after a teenager was shot by police in Athens on 6 December 2008.

events.title: Gaza War
events.description: Israel began a military operation in the Gaza Strip on 27 December 2008.

events.title: Gas crisis
events.description: Russia stopped gas supplies to Ukraine on 1 January 2009; supplies to several European countries were cut off for about two weeks.

events.title: Recovery Act
events.description: President Barack Obama signed the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act on 17 February 2009.

source.title: Wikipedia: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009

events.title: L'Aquila earthquake
events.description: An earthquake struck L'Aquila, Italy, on 6 April 2009.

events.title: End of the Sri Lankan civil war
events.description: The Sri Lankan government declared victory over the Tamil Tigers in May 2009.

events.title: Second North Korean nuclear test
events.description: North Korea conducted a second nuclear test on 25 May 2009.

events.title: Swine flu pandemic
events.description: The World Health Organization declared the H1N1 swine flu outbreak a pandemic in June 2009.

events.title: Election protests
events.description: Mass protests against the announced result of the presidential election broke out in Iran from June 2009.

events.title: Air France Flight 447
events.description: Air France Flight 447 from Rio de Janeiro to Paris crashed into the Atlantic Ocean on 1 June 2009.

events.title: Coup in Honduras
events.description: The Honduran army removed President Manuel Zelaya from office on 28 June 2009.

events.title: Ürümqi riots
events.description: Riots broke out in Ürümqi, Xinjiang, on 5 July 2009.

events.title: Treaty of Lisbon in force
events.description: The Treaty of Lisbon entered into force on 1 December 2009.

events.title: Copenhagen climate summit
events.description: The United Nations climate conference opened in Copenhagen on 7 December 2009.
